facts.text: Noblesville was platted in January 1823 by William Conner and Josiah Polk and likely named after James Noble, the first U.S. Senator from Indiana.
The town’s historic courthouse, the county seat’s landmark, sits in downtown Noblesville and reflects the city’s long civic heritage.
In 1927 Forest Park opened as Noblesville’s first major city park, and a public pool followed in 1931, giving residents early access to outdoor recreation.
Conner Prairie, a living history museum south of Noblesville, preserves the 1823 home of founder William Conner among other pioneer buildings.
Noblesville’s railroad history began in 1851 when the Indianapolis and Peru Railroad arrived, marking the town’s growth into a regional hub.
The city hosts the Riverview Health Arena at Innovation Mile, where the NBA G League affiliate, the Noblesville Boom, plays home games.
